long_biography.plain_text:
Raised on British Columbia’s Salt Spring Island, Kevin Smith grew up sailing and chose jobs that kept him on the water. He trained as a geographer, worked as a marine park ranger and spent five years negotiating the Great Bear Rainforest land-use plan. In 2001, the owners of Maple Leaf Adventures mentored Smith and transferred the small expedition company to him.

Smith and his wife, Maureen Gordon, expanded Maple Leaf from one heritage schooner and a limited sailing schedule into a three-ship coastal tourism operator. He remained hands-on as captain, expedition leader and chief executive while developing conservation partnerships with Indigenous communities and industry peers. During the pandemic, he helped organize a collaborative marine-debris cleanup that kept crews working and extended the company’s stewardship model beyond passenger voyages.

Raised on British Columbia’s Salt Spring Island, Kevin Smith grew up sailing and chose jobs that kept him on the water. He trained as a geographer, worked as a marine park ranger and spent five years negotiating the Great Bear Rainforest land-use plan. In 2001, the owners of Maple Leaf Adventures mentored Smith and transferred the small expedition company to him.

Smith and his wife, Maureen Gordon, expanded Maple Leaf from one heritage schooner and a limited sailing schedule into a three-ship coastal tourism operator. He remained hands-on as captain, expedition leader and chief executive while developing conservation partnerships with Indigenous communities and industry peers. During the pandemic, he helped organize a collaborative marine-debris cleanup that kept crews working and extended the company’s stewardship model beyond passenger voyages.
